notes.title: Season 4.5 Update - "Dark Essence"
notes.content:
[p][b]We're thrilled to introduce Season 4.5. This season brings the mysterious Dark Bosses, extends the Underrealm to unprecedented depths, introduces powerful Tier 5 equipment, and delivers a comprehensive rebalancing of the entire modification system. Prepare for darker challenges and greater rewards.[/b][/p][h3][b]

[/b]🕯️ [b]Tuesday, August 12th at 1:00 PM EST[/b] –[b]Chaos Days[/b] begin![/h3][p]
 The servers will go down briefly (up to 1 hour) as we prep for the new season.
 Seasonal characters will be wiped, so don’t forget to [i]migrate[/i] the ones you want to keep into [b]Offline Mode[/b]!

 🎁 [b]Bonus[/b]: Everyone who participates in Chaos Days will receive the [b]exclusive Ride of Swordie'm Mount[/b]! [/p][p][/p][h3]🧿 [b]Friday, August 15th at 1:00 PM EST[/b] – [b]Season 4.5: Dark Essence[/b] officially begins![/h3][p]
 The update will be live 1 hour before launch so you’ll have time to get ready.

notes.title: Season 4: Rise of the Necromancer

[h2]Season 4 launches on May 25th![/h2]
[b]The gates will open at 1PM EST[/b]
Rise with the Dwarves, command the dead — jump in, forge your legend. The Realms await you champion!

[previewyoutube=CoHZaAzlJDg;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1][b]Stone and Darkness unite![/b][/h1]
In Season 4: Rise of the Necromancer, warriors old and new must rise to meet the challenge.

This season, the Realms crack open wider than ever before. Step through the Time Tear and back into an era lost to ruin—where ancient powers still walk the land, and the Dwarves have yet to fall. 
[h3][b]New Races[/b][/h3]
With the introduction of two new playable races, the mighty Dwarves and the vengeful Graveborn, players now choose from four distinct ancestries, each offering unique bonuses to weapon types and elemental affinities. Build your legend with the might of forged steel or the fury of the grave.

[h3] [b]New Necromancer Stance[/b] [/h3]
At the heart of the new season is the debut of the Necromancer class, a master of death who commands a legion of minions. Unlike traditional brawlers or spellcasters, the Necromancer reshapes the battlefield through his undead army—empowering skeletal warriors, spectral beasts, and horrific abominations to overwhelm the enemies of the Realms. It's a bold new playstyle for those who prefer strategy, positioning, and relentless pressure over raw damage.

[h3] [b]New Home Fort[/b] [/h3]
The Home-Fort has been reborn. No longer the shining cathedral of previous seasons, the fort now reflects a world mid-collapse—a war-torn stronghold clinging to hope. Cracked stone, shattered banners, and flickers of dwarven resilience tell the story of a people on the edge... and a future not yet written.

[*] New Feature: Expeditions - The [i]Fortune Assistant [/i]has left the Home Fort, and [i]Kordrim the Explorer[/i] has taken his place. Kordrim will gladly take your keys to the Tomb of Fortune, Catacombs, Grave Digger's Cove, and the Elven Capital - and go fetch the loot for you in a matter of seconds. 

[*] New Feature: Multiple rewards in Boss Encounters - Upon entering a boss encounter, Amen'non the Ancient will now appear if the player has more keys to the same encounter. Players can now trade the additional keys with this ancient being, which will use them to enhance the rewards, should the boss be defeated.

[*] New Feature: Boss scaling selection - Boss encounters will now scale the same as Ruptures. After defeating a Boss Encounter, you may choose to battle again in the same level or push higher levels, for better rewards. Upgrading the Rupture Portal through the Home Fort Giant will also affect how many levels you can skip in Boss encounters.

[*] New Feature: Home Fort stash - The stash chests that used to spread out through the fort have been replaced with a single, multiple tab stash. [b] Important Notice[/b]: This change will delete all items stored in the current stash system. Players should take out any items they wish to keep from the stash [b]Before[/b] downloading the new season patch.

Hey Adventurers! We've got an exciting update packed with new features, balance changes, and bugfixes.
Check out what's new in Season 3.5 of Dwarven Realms - Awakening:

[h2]NEW FEATURES IN SEASON 3.5 - AWAKENING[/h2] 
[h3]INTRODUCING JUGGERNAUTS: THE FISTS STANCE [/h3]
Unleash your inner brawler with our brand-new FISTS class!
This powerful new combat style lets you pummel enemies with devastating close-range attacks.
Wield new specialized Fist Weapons with unique aesthetics.
Master an exciting combo system that rewards skillful play. Chain attacks to build combo points, then unleash devastating finishers. 
[h3]NEW RACE - ORC:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Customize your character with race-specific clothing and appearance options
[*] Unlock racial traits that boost certain combat styles as you progress. (Applies to Humans as well)
[*] Crush Everything with a new playable race - The Orcs! and harness their natural strength and resilience in battle.
[/list]
[h3]PRIME ELITE ENCOUNTERS[/h3]
Face the ultimate challenge with our new Prime Elite mechanics: Elite enemies have a chance to spawn as a significantly more powerful 'Prime' variant of themselves.
[list]
[*] Encounter unique and enhanced attack patterns from Prime Elites
[*] Prime Elites have a lot more health and deal more damage  
[*] Prime Elites feature spectacular visual effects to distinguish them
[/list]
[h2]GAMEPLAY[/h2]
[list]
[*] Improved Cave Crasher's Rock Trail effects.
[*] Added tooltips to Essence Turn-in.
[*] Renamed Charging affinity to Momentum.
[*] Introduced a new affinity: Hazard - to allow for better distribution of affinities across offhands.
[*] Health Regeneration% stat now increases the player's base health regeneration - instead of adding a % of health as flat regeneration.
[*] Default Rupture Containers no longer drop equipment.
[*] Experience gained through Research Table (Scrolls, Tablets, and Books) has been reduced.
[*] Experience bonus gained from upgrading the Research Table significantly increased.
[*] Flat Damage can now only appear as a base affix for Weapons.
[*] Reduced the number of items that drop in Ruptures.
[*] Increased Qhik'zichar mount drop rate.
[/list]
[h3]META / BALANCE CHANGES[/h3]
[list]
[*] We've updated the formulas for enemy health scaling and player damage calculation to improve balance and progression.
Enemy health now scales more dynamically based on difficulty, while player damage calculations have been refined to ensure smoother power growth across levels.

[*] As part of the effort to get more diverse playstyles, we've disconnected the hard link between specific stats and stances. Basically allowing players to combine any stance with any stat distribution.
 [list]
 [*] Removed the stat scaling bonuses from Stance Proficiency
 [*] Legendary (purple) items can now roll with any of the 7 stat attributes.      
 [/list]  
[*] As with every season, we've made updates to Offhand Abilities and Monograms. Also Stance Attacks have undergone a refinement of Damage and Energy costs. You can review the full details below
[/list]

[h2]BUGFIXES[/h2]
[list]
[*] Potions will now only be collected if the player an empty potion slot
[*] Celestial forge can no longer be closed unexpectedly
[*] Improved visuals for epic antler weapon containers
[*] Fixed an issue where lightning beam was not attached to the player
[/list]

[h2]USER INTERFACE[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added equipment slot-type filtering
[*] Limited loot popup on lower right of screen to 10 rows maximum
[*] "Unlearn" option in skill tree only appears after using at least one skill point
[*] Added Infused rupture selector overlay
[*] Added search box to mounts, pets and skins lists
[/list]

[h3]Offhand Balance Updates:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Arcane Apocalypse:[/b][list]
[*] Damage multiplier increased (0.84 → 0.93).
[*] Buff mod: Chance to gain buff increased by 10% (15% → 25%). Buff now grants 150% Arcane Damage.
[*] Explode Twice mod: Chance to trigger increased by 10% (10% → 20%). [/list]
[*] [b]Arcane Orb:[/b][list]
[*] Chaos Orbs mod: Damage bonus increased to 25% (20% → 25%).
[*] Burst mod: Now gains +10% damage per extra orb.[/list]
[*] [b]Electric Dragons:[/b][list]
[*] Meteor mod: Chance to trigger increased to 20% (10% → 20%).
[*] Meteor mod: Damage increased to 80% (40% → 80%).
[*] Extra Dragon & Range mod: Now grants Area affinity. [/list]
[*] [b]Ferocity of Wolves:[/b]
[list]
[*] Leap mod: Bonus damage per leap reduced to 35% (50% → 35%).
[/list]

notes.title: Season 0.24 Eternal Peaks
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We’re thrilled to announce the new season of Dwarven Realms: Eternal Peaks, launching this Friday, June 28th at 1 PM EST.

Eternal Peaks is our most ambitious season to date, with nearly every aspect of the game revamped. This includes the introduction of permanent characters, controller support, offline mode, a new UI, new end game progression systems, additions to crafting, and much more.

Here are some of the highlights from the Season 0.24 Patch Notes. We’ll add more details as we get closer to Friday:

[list]
[*] Permanent Characters: One of our most requested features ever. For players who prefer a non-seasonal experience and want to stick with their character forever, you can now create permanent characters.

[*] Controller Support: Another highly requested feature. While we're still ironing out a few things, you should now be able to play smoothly with a controller.

[*] Offline Mode: Many of you have asked for the ability to play without an internet connection, free from leaderboard competition. You can now enjoy the game offline.

[*] Revamped Rupture Gateways: We’ve merged the rupture and special dungeon gates into a single gateway, and created a map of the realms. This enhances storytelling, showcases the world, and highlights the amount of content available.

[*] UI Overhaul (Work in Progress): We've started revamping the menus, fonts, buttons, and more to make the interface more welcoming and user-friendly. This is part of a larger project, with continued improvements planned in the coming weeks.

[*] New Crafting Station: We've transformed the old throne into a new codex system. You can now upgrade yellow items to orange and select the exact modifiers you want.

[*] Improved Guidance for New Players: New screens now guide first-time players through the basic gameplay experience.

[*] Experimental Game Cinematics: We're testing new cinematics with voiceovers from a hobbyist game actor and AI-generated imagery. This aims to enhance the narrative and deepen player engagement with the story.

[*] New End Game Skills: We've added new skills for stances that were missing them. Dual wield for 1H stances, a bubble for Mauls and Staves, mirage archers for Archers, shadow mage abilities for Mages, a deadly round attack for Spears, and a new enraged mechanic for 2H.

[*] New End Game Progression System: We're building a new system to allow better end game progression with collected resources. Players can now turn in resources to increase faction with the elves and upgrade the elven capital.

[*] Ruptures Environment Overhaul: We've reworked most of the rupture environments to be more compelling and performant, with changes to earlier ruptures and continued updates throughout the season.

[*] Bug Fixes and Optimization: Tons of bug fixes and much better game performance and optimization.

[*] Audio Overhaul: We’ve remade and added numerous new audio effects for all attacks and abilities, aiming to revamp the entire game’s audio for launch.

[*] End Game Fellowship Progression (Work in Progress): More details will be shared soon.

[*] Tear Drops in Ruptures: Tear Drops now appear randomly in ruptures. Activating them will spawn mobs and a promised elite mob that drops a chest, making grinding more fun and essence collection faster.

possible.

notes.title: Season 20: Shadowforge
notes.content:
Before talking about patch notes, we’d like to share a few things with the Dwarven Realms community, especially as it started to grow substantially lately.

In creating Dwarven Realms, my brother and I embarked on a unique journey driven by our shared passion for building something different. Unlike other ARPGs backed by teams of dozens if not hundreds of devs, with hundreds of millions in budget, we are just a duo of novice game developers, navigating uncharted territories in game development.

Video games are developed through cycles. The initial development cycle almost always occurs "behind closed doors" and is released only when the studio decides it's ready. While "early access" on Steam is very common - it means different things in different games. Dwarven Realms is a [b]genuine early-access game[/b]. This means it currently resembles more of a pre-alpha stage you’d see in larger studios built games. 

In Dwarven Realms the community takes part in the active development cycle. We treat our community as part of the dev team, we take feedback very seriously, and the folks actively playing are essentially part of the team.

This has many different implications, and we have to pay a price to move at the speed we’re moving, some of the trade offs we are making include the following:

[list]
[*] Data backward compatibility: The fact that the core systems change rapidly also affects all data models. Trying to keep backward compatibility or data migration will cause the game development and changes to crystalize and freeze. Until the game's core loop is established, wiping data is just too important. We constantly revisit the concept of permanent characters, which will be implemented when Dwarven Realms expands in size, stability, and complexity.

[*] Patch notes: When a game is stable, and the meta slightly changes from version to version, it is easy to update and keep patch notes. Furthermore, the player base expects this. Dwarven Realms changes in its core from every season in very short release cycles. This means everything changes. Items, Systems, Modifiers, Skills, Abilities, Enemies, Progression rate, experience, build, and almost everything in the game. Keeping detailed, updated patch notes in such an early game is impossible.

[*] Mid-season changes. While a stable meta is required for an ARPG with a competitive element, stabilizing the meta only from season to season will drastically slow down game development. 
[/list]

We see the frustration from some players who expect from Dwarven Realms the same things they’d expect from a triple-A game on Steam, even though it is in early access, and even for its  very low price tag. We want to emphasize that Dwarven Realms is not for everyone in its current state. Some gamers love participating in this early point and feel their direct contribution to the game, while others want a more polished product. It's a journey, and it’s your choice whether to take part in it or not. We hope you'd join this journey with us.

Now, to Shadowforge. This season promises to reshape the game's meta, introducing meaningful changes to mods, progression, new abilities and challenging bosses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42825438/a5d76ccc6f623d0d400662d2abbdaf8c51b0a7b7.png[/img]

Season 20 Patch Notes:
[list]
[*] We are introducing a new end-game event called Shadowforge. This event will help players get a substantial amount of materials to craft end-game bracers and let players find the powerful modifiers bracers offer so they can reach their desired end-game build. 
[*] We have revamped ruptured levels 1 to 15, introducing more challenging boss fights with new bosses' abilities. 
[*] Unique mobs that spawn in ruptures will now have special abilities, making them more exciting yet more challenging. 
[*] We are introducing new container mechanics. Instead of random containers being spread out everywhere, mobs will now have a chance to drop containers. Containers will be rarer but also have more value and better loot. There will be multiple container types.
[*] This solves the problem of having to click on containers many times (based on player's requests)
[*] It also solves the meta of players going in and out of ruptures just to hunt for damage-reduction gems or dragonling cages, for example. They will randomly spawn as you kill mobs. 
[*] We are now introducing rupture-scaled loot. This will apply to the entire boss chest, including stance fragments. It will also include receiving more bags of essences from higher-level rupture statutes, making pushing higher ruptures valid.
[*] We made adjustments and balanced the cards. Crit chance and pure damage cards have been nerfed, and others have been boosted to even the playing field and make things more balanced (based on the player's requests)
[*] There is now a male/female character creation screen. (Based on player's requests from both genders)
[*] All infused chests and Akkorus' chests are now gated behind the boss kill. You will have to kill the boss to get the reward. This will stop low-level characters from running the level 100 Akkorus map just for the stones. (Based on player's requests)
[*] Lightning totems have gotten a slight nerf, making it more balanced with the rest of the abilities. Our goal is to make it still a fun, viable build but more in line with the rest of the abilities. Changes include the time they stay on the screen and the number of times they strike. Also, balance the proc and damage their off-hands offer. 
[*] More audio was polished and fixed, making some skills that triggered sounds constantly playable.
[*] All tier 2 item sets in Akkorus maps will require more oaks and will be harder to obtain. You will also find these vendors outside Akkorus, Min Loduhr, and Olympus.
[*] Dash has been split from space and now has a dedicated button, and players can bind it to whatever they want. It also takes 0.2s instead of 0.4s.
[*] Turning chat off in options (based on streamer's requests)
[*] Akkorus and Elven, Slug ruptures keys, are rare, making them much more meaningful. We closed the loophole from last season of FS having endless slug ruptures.
[*] You can now block Fellowships invites in settings (based on popular streamer requests)
[*] Archery will no longer require arrows.
[*] We are introducing non-FS bracer mods, making it viable for players who want to progress without an FS. Making Fellowships and Non-Fellowships characters on par isn't a goal; it's OK that folks in FS have a slight advantage; the long-term solution for this would be different leagues/ladders.
[/list]

notes.content:

Our current season has been extended by an extra three weeks, giving you more time to delve into the wonders of Dwarven Realms! Reach level 10, join our discord, and claim your very own Elder Stag of the Myrahnian Druids Mount for free. But that's not all! AS season 17 is now underway, a reminder it will be an extended one, lasting for four weeks. Here are some essential points to keep in mind:

While we acknowledge that there's still a lot to be done in terms of fixes, tweaks, and balance, we're focusing on two key pillars for this release: Gameplay and Core Loop, and Performance.

Gameplay Changes:
Jump Removal: After testing the game without the jump feature, we found that gameplay becomes more challenging and realistic. The absence of jumping requires players to be mindful of their position, heightening the action and difficulty.

Rupture Mob Grinding: 
We're revamping the base loop for mob grinding in ruptures. Mobs will now spawn in waves that gradually increase with an RNG factor. The longer you stay in a rupture and grind, the more enemies you'll face. However, after reaching a peak point, the numbers will decrease until the next peak. This dynamic system introduces strategic challenges, especially in higher-level ruptures.

Mob Stacking: 
Basic melee mobs can now stack on top of each other, adding an extra layer of complexity. Combined with the removal of jumping, this forces players to be mindful of their position and stay vigilant against incoming enemies.

Performance Changes:
We've overhauled how enemies behave on a technical level, with most changes meant to be seamless. However, as this rewrite affects a significant portion of the game, be prepared for potential breaking bugs. If you encounter any oddities during gameplay or combat, please let us know, and we'll address them promptly.

Note for Hardcore Players: If you're on a hardcore character, consider waiting before updating, starting a new test character, or preparing for a challenging experience. Be aware of potential risks and embrace the changes cautiously.

As always there might be more changes or fixes that we overlooked or forgot to add so stay vigilant. Additionaly these changes are just a base line that will allow us to add and change a lot of other features that we want to introduce later.

Thank you for being part of the Dwarven Realms community! Your support and feedback are invaluable as we continue to shape and improve the game.

Once again, thank you all for your fantastic support! If you have any questions, feel free to message me anytime. Your participation makes Dwarven Realms an incredible journey for everyone involved.

notes.title: Season XIV Fortress of Time
notes.content:
Hey everyone, season 14 of DR will be launching shortly. 
One of the biggest challenges we've noticed among new players is that the campaign doesn't reflect DR's endgame. It also made us focus our limited resources and always make choices on what's more important, investing in our campaign or investing in our endless ruptures loop. We have found a compromise where we essentially rupturized the campaign, or in other words, the campaign will be played in the same style as ruptures. It also made crafting and unlocking progress in the campaign more meaningful.

Here is what to expect in the new season:

[list]
[*] You will begin in your home fort in the snowy mountains. Home fort has been remade.
[*] There are multiple new boss fights to make the campaign more fun and meaningful. 
[*] Fight through ruptures in the zones you know and Love.
[*] Crafting recipes, offhand, bracers, relics, and jewelry will all unlock as you progress through the first 35 ruptures. Rupture 36 will seem very familiar to the previous endgame.
[/list]

Changes to End Game: 
[list]
[*] Opening ruptures no longer require keys.
[*] So, there is no selection of rupture zone. Instead, you will be teleported randomly to one of the 24 ruptures.
[*] Since progression is different and ruptures scale faster, we will reduce the rupture level of high-end zones such as the Olympus, bridge, etc. 
[/list]

As always, don't be alarmed by the changes. We constantly try new things to improve, and everything is temporary. These changes affect all aspects of the game. Therefore, the progression is different. Whether it is too slow or too fast, it will still be tweaked many times.

notes.title: Season XI.5 Kingdom of Akkorus
notes.content:
We're releasing a new balance patch to season XI, along side new content. 

- We have balanced (or at least did our best) mob and rupture progression to match stats, experience, and item progression. The flow of the game should feel better, yet slower. We are fine with people reaching level 600, and completing ruptures level 500, but it should be more challenging and generally take longer.
- We have added new fellowship features and content. Once you are part of a fellowship, you will see a new map in the fellowship hall at your home fort. Unlocking the new zones is done by leveling up the fellowship. Finding a key to the new content is a rare rupture drop, and will drop to fellowships that are grinding together. 
- Offhands now have auto sort and will not be disenchanted automatically
- Skill tree has new nodes with fixed stats and fewer inventory slots. Also, all buffs have been rebalanced to the new game progression.
- We have gotten rid of the stance gems conversion. You will now find Stance Fractures and be able to craft your specific stance gems from that resource.
- Multiple bug fixes, including weird camera issues, lighting, item stats, and more.
- Boss arenas will now have significantly fewer adds, and a lot more containers for a dump of the essence before you leave.
- The mobs not having aggro while a player is mounted on specific mounts is hopefully fixed.

notes.title: Season XI, Kingdom of Akkorus
notes.content:
- We have been continuing our journey to improve the progression of characters. Item's stats, player's stats (and hp) have all been reworked, we also introduced a couple of new stats. While the numbers will start out much lower, the progression of the game will seem familiar. 
- We have removed pure stat bonuses from fossils. You will still find small/large gems across the campaign, ruptures, dungeons, catacombs etc and you can still improve all of your stats as before, only now it's % based. 
- The proc abilities have been removed from the skill tree. There is now new magical items slots that will allow you to choose which abilities you'd like to equip. You will run into them early in the campaign.
- Scrolls, books and tablets will give significantly less experience. Slaying mobs will now be the fastest way to level. This is true for both the campaign and in ruptures.
- There is a new rare mob called Amadora the Explorer. It spawns in campaign and ruptures, slaying it will grant you temporary great power.
- Lootbags drop rate in ruptures have been buffed.
- Mobs in ruptures will now drop essence orbs. Every 10 essence orbs will allow you to open a container. This means you will have to slay mobs in ruptures in order to open containers.
- All mobs in ruptures are now melee mobs. Ranged mobs will spawn in ruptures but as a single mob spawn once in X spawners. Sort of how time slimes spawn works today. 
- Time slimes will be more rare, and add less time. This will make it harder to stay in the same rupture forever.
- Large Slimes will be significantly more rare. 
- New zones are still been worked on, and will not be released on launch, but throughout the first and second weeks of the season. 

We believe these changes will help us set the right foundations to build a more interesting itemization system and builds system in the up coming seasons. This will also set the right tone for us to make ruptures dynamics more fun and interesting, and find a balance between slaying mobs, and running through them for containers/slimes/bosses. Please feel free to send us any meaningful feedback as you play through the new season.

notes.title: Dwarven Realms - Season 7
notes.content:
Today we will launch Season 7 - The Clash of the Elements. It is fair to say that since the first time we launched Dwarven Realms for early access back in December of last year, this is the first season we completely don't know what is going to happen. There was just too many stuff to test. Which means we honestly have no idea how the game plays out. We could wait another week and deliver more predictable content but as you already know us, we much rather do it with you.

We think true balance is a very delicate art which even in simple games could take years and millions of data points. With that being said this season doesn't have any kind of data. The game could be way harder or way easier we can't even tell. This is why we decided this season will last for a duration of one week. After that we will try to stabilize all the new features and modifiers and start another 3 week season to work on more content.

Skills
The majority of the time has been taken to overhaul the skill tree. There is not much point in trying to explain it since its a completely new tree. The major difference from the previous seasons we hope to see is people will have different builds. Every skill will belong to 1 of 3 elements - Fire, Lightning, and Arcane, and will benefit from such bonuses accordingly, if you have any. We hope to have a lot more mechanics based on these elements in the future.

Stances
We added a basic playstyle for archery and magery.
The magery shoots AoE from Wands and has 2 unique abilities. One causes an explosion around you and the other will fire a volley of your normal attack.
The archer fire bows with 2 unique shots. The first will cause your arrow to explode and the second will fire an arrow to the sky, where it will split into a lot of arrows which cause the ground to rain with arrows.
The different skills for stances will no longer be on the skill tree and will now progress with time use. The way the progression feels will certainly change next season so don't get to worried if its too fast or too slow.

Items
Items have not changed much but there are a few new modifiers. Lower tier items will drop modifiers for lower tier skills.

As always. There was a lot of work and a lot of changes in a very short amount of time. This might have a lot of gameplay issues and bugs. If you prefer to enjoy a more stable experience, please wait and play the season next week after we had a chance to let the dust settle down. Some of changes and tweaks have been made to some of the current content.
If you have requests regarding the new systems, or want to report bugs feel free to do it in the correct discord forums. We would welcome these with open arms.

Some future plans regarding the new content
After careful thoughts and considerations we think that the experience we want to provide for each stance needs to be very unique. So the game stays as it was, each stance has a minor mechanic which makes it more special. To make a stance really play differently will require a full season of effort for each stance by it self. In the future we plan to do exactly that, spend a full season on one stance, and remake them 1 by 1. This includes making a crafting/tools stance with different mechanics making tools viable and interesting.
Items are still in the same place they were. They require a more sophisticated overhaul in order to be interesting. The potential for crafting in Dwarven Realms is huge, with survival elements, crafting lists, and different mechanics they have attached to them. Until we work on a better crafting system the items will keep being modified slowly.

notes.title: Season 5 Launch
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42825438/93e21292257cb07d558875eafc02ec59dccf073c.png[/img]

Greetings Realm Warriors. Season 5- Shadow Wield – is now LIVE!

As we are still in our search for stability, smooth game flow, and a bug free world, this season includes a lot of fixes and quality of life changes. Some are minor but have been requested by players, and some are massive, like stabilizing the data saving and loading system.

As we are progressing fast, we are constantly “breaking” the game from season to season. It also makes it very hard to keep a detailed change log of all changes. We are also unsure if we want the players to obsess with every meta-gaming mechanic from season to season.

We are constantly trying to make the game more fun every season. Some changes will be left up to the community to discover. Below are the major ones we will announce:

[list]
[*] Major change in the 4 stances. One of the things we would like to test this season is a proof of concept that different playstyles are viable and people enjoy them. Before we go on a new crusade to rebuild stances, add archery and magery, and add many skills - we decided to give each stance a different variation with the current tools the game already offers. So we added an end game skill to each stance skill tree. Have fun testing them out and reporting changes and suggestions. (Minor balances to these changes might be introduced mid season!)
[*] Items. As a long journey to keep balancing items, making them both exciting and viable, major changes into the item generation system have been made. Although most of them should be transparent to the players, we hope this season you will definitely see more changes. Crafting also took a small step into becoming a little bit more viable strategy. It is also important to note that the crafting system still needs a lot of work and will also get a strong overhaul after the new skill system.
[*] Progression. This is a very tricky subject. On one hand for some players progression seems extremely easy and fast, while for others we hear that it's extremely slow and hard. The bottom line is, if you put in a lot more time you will obviously progress more as in every game in this genre. There is simply no way to unlock all game mechanics and enter “god mode” with just a few hours of gameplay. To balance this lower ruptures will now yield significantly less books than higher level ruptures.
[*] Data. We have separated the save flow into 2 different critical flows. One for the character and one for the world. This will hopefully reduce the size of the character data to be much smaller and a lot more consistent. We hope this will cause players who suffered from data loss to experience this much much less. But as was stated before, it is only a small step on the way to keep all data backed up and saved on the server side which will eliminate cheating and data loss forever. (As a side effect, your map table, workbench, mortar and furnace state in the home fort will now be saved if you leave and return! woohoo)
[/list]

On the topic of cheating and exploits. All cheating, exploits and meta breaking bugs should be reported instantly. If you are using an exploit to gain an unfair advantage that is clearly not a viable strategy you are mature enough to be aware of it. You are only cheating your friends, the community, and yourself - and you will be banned unless you report it right away.

If you have messed around with the save file or decided to try and cheat and you have been banned -> and you would like to compete fair next season, please message us in discord and we will evaluate and unban you if needed.

If you are in the top players for last season and for some reason don’t see your new mount a few hours after the new season starts, please message us on Discord!

Next Seasons:
[list]
[*] As our resources and time are very limited and there is literally a roadmap for at least 2 years we need to focus our efforts effectively. The plan for the upcoming weeks:
[*] We will focus on building a versatile skill tree which will require more decision making by the player. This will also include changes to how skills are unlocked and opened. It will also include 2 (hopefully 3?) new stances. Magery and Archery. It is extremely important to us to make these mechanics fun. If they are, they will be balanced and if not we will remove and try something new.
[*] Large World bosses. Bosses with unique mechanics and abilities that will actually require a lot more versatile game play to defeat.
[*] Crafting system. Once the items make sense and end world content is balanced we will revamp the entire crafting system. We want the elements of grind, survival with various loot to open up a progression of crafting more unique items and modifiers.
[*] Data. As stated many times before. We will not rest until data is consistent and stable for everyone forever.
[*] GPU/CPU and FPS rate. This is more of an art than a science. The game needs to be examined under a microscope until every performance and optimization option has been thoroughly tested and improved.
[*] New end game maps dungeons.
[*] Fixing all current ruptures. This includes environmental issues, look and feel, spawners and more. 
[*] Moving to 3 weeks seasons. As more content is added and the game is more stable we would move into 3 weeks seasons. This will allow players to spend more time with their character and progress, while giving us a lot more room to push meaningful content and changes.
[/list]

notes.title: Season 3 - The Fossil of the Ancient Demigods
notes.content:
Hail to you Realm Warriors. 
Season 3 - The Fossil of the Ancient Demigods is live!
[img]https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/769933877601894413/1060937469631139880/season-title.png[/img]

Even though creating content is our dream - if the game is not stable or balanced it is all in vain. Ergo this season was centered mainly around bug fixes, meta stabalization, UI enhancement and quality of life fixes.

As we are moving fast, pulling the rug from both sides, and pushing rapidly - we are not able to really track down every little change that the game is going through. 
However, these are the main points this season revolves around.

* Trying to enhance and fix FPS and choppiness. As long as an ARPG has lag all else is futile.
*  Skills. As fun as it is to click a button and see everything exploding - this requires a bit of effort - having a full build of all skills will require more amount of effort
*  Energy/Energy Regeneration and Critical Chance - these attributes have been given out much too fast and in much too greater scale, we have tried to make them balanced more.
*  Mobs behaviour and aggressiveness - we have identified a major bug causing the wierd behaviour and it is partly fix though still under works.
*  Many (many many) bug fixes. The biggest one is having your data lost some times or not saving in Ruptures when quiting to Menu. We can't stress enough how thankful we are for the communities help on this.
*  End game. Being stuck and not having how/where to advance to is frustrating. The main reason is currently due to the game being extremely new and lacking content. Until more content is released we will try to provide more ways to advance.

In the spirit of the Holidays, the top 25 warriors on the leaderboards will be granted a Harmoniyan Rain Deer mount

NEXT SEASONS - 
Number 1 priority is always the fairnesss, fun, and balance of the meta. Assuming these are stable - here are some of the plans for the next few seasons
*  More enhancements and new stuff revolving crafting and itemizations. Unique items that give more abilities and skills.
*  Re-make of the entire skill system and skill tree. A lot more options and variations of play style.
*  Re-make of the stances including adding Archery and Magery. Although hit+roll mechanics is fun, we intend for each stance to have a lot more depth (dual wield? who knows?)
*  A lot more content - new dungeons, new lands and new enemies to destroy. This also  includes a lot more depth in ruptures.
*  Boss fights -  a lot more mechanics to make the engagements more than a stand-and-damage fight.
